shots.desc: Short orbit over the page: a city with a temple court on the right, a house with an upstairs room on the left, a road along the front. From the right, Jesus rides in on a little donkey, His friends walking behind; two sellers shout in the temple court.
People pour out along the road waving palm branches; coats and branches appear on the road in front of the donkey. Jesus waves from the donkey; Peter waves his palm branch higher than anyone.
At the bend by the temple gate the procession stops. Jesus answers the grumblers from the donkey; Peter bends down to a heap of roadside stones and listens.
The temple court: stalls, cages of doves, piles of coins; the two sellers shout prices. Jesus steps in through the gate and stops; His face grows sad. The donkey grazes outside by the house.
Jesus, firm, tips the money table over: coins roll everywhere. He opens the dove cages: the doves fly up and away. The sellers scramble. Nobody is hurt.
Evening. The upstairs room: a low table set for supper, a bench along the wall, lamps. The four disciples stand in the middle and squabble, chests out. Jesus stands quietly at the back by the basin.
Night, lamps lit. The disciples sit on the bench along the wall with dusty feet. Jesus quietly ties a towel round His waist, pours water into a bowl, carries it over and kneels in front of Andrew.
Jesus moves along the bench to Peter and kneels. Peter jerks his feet back, waving his hands; then throws out his hands and pushes his head forward: wash all of me!
Jesus stands up with the towel still round His waist and speaks to them all. The four look at each other, a bit ashamed.
At the low table, lamps glowing. Jesus, in the middle, takes the round flat bread, looks up and thanks God, breaks it and passes it to His friends.
Jesus lifts the cup with both hands. A soft warm glow. The disciples are very still.
Peter gets up, picks up the towel and the water jug, and kneels down in front of his brother Andrew. Andrew giggles; James and John grin and nudge each other.
The whole page at night: the lit upstairs room with Jesus and His friends at the table, the quiet temple court, the donkey dozing by the house. A warm glow from the room.

lines.zh: 逾越节快到了，好多人去耶路撒冷过节。耶稣也来了，不骑高头大马，骑的是一头小驴。
lines.en: Passover was near, and crowds went up to Jerusalem. Jesus came too, not on a proud horse, but on a little donkey.
lines.dir: storyteller opening, bright; a smile and a little surprise on 小驴 / 'a little donkey'

lines.zh: 大家都跑出来欢迎他，挥着棕树枝，把衣服铺在路上。
lines.en: People ran out to welcome Him, waving palm branches and spreading their coats on the road.
lines.dir: lively, building; quicker on the second half

lines.zh: 和散那！欢迎我们的王！他是上帝派来的！
lines.en: Hosanna! Hooray for our King! God has sent Him!
lines.dir: crowd of 8-10 incl. children, joyful, overlapping; a child's voice on top

lines.zh: 哈哈，大家都知道他是王啦！我们也要当大人物了！
lines.en: Ha ha! Everyone knows He's the King! Soon we'll be important too!
lines.dir: bursting with pride, waving the palm; big grin on 大人物 / 'important'

lines.zh: 有几个宗教领袖不高兴：老师，快叫他们安静！
lines.en: Some leaders grumbled: 'Teacher, make them be quiet!'
lines.dir: the grumble in a lower, prim voice; not scary

lines.zh: 我告诉你们，他们要是不出声，这些石头都会喊起来！
lines.en: I tell you, if they keep quiet, these stones will shout out!
lines.dir: calm and sure, a twinkle in it; not cross

lines.zh: 石头……会喊？喂，石头，你说句话呀？
lines.en: The stones... would shout? Hey, stone! Say something!
lines.dir: puzzled, then leaning in and whispering to the stone, very comic

lines.zh: 卖鸽子咯！便宜卖啦——嗯，其实也不太便宜！
lines.en: Doves! Doves for sale! Cheap, cheap! ...Well, not that cheap!
lines.dir: loud market cry, then a sly aside to himself; comic, not nasty

lines.zh: 圣殿是祷告的地方，可现在吵得像菜市场，还有人骗钱。
lines.en: God's house was for praying. But now it was as noisy as a market, and some sellers cheated.
lines.dir: quieter, a little sad; slow on 上帝的家 / 'God's house'

lines.zh: 这是我父的家！是让大家祷告的地方，不是骗钱的地方！
lines.en: This is My Father's house, a place for everyone to pray, not to cheat people!
lines.dir: firm and strong, clear; sad underneath, never shouting in rage

lines.zh: 哎呀，我的钱！别滚，别滚啦！
lines.en: Oh no, my money! Stop rolling! Stop rolling!
lines.dir: comic panic, bent double chasing coins

lines.zh: 我的鸽子……都飞走啦！
lines.en: My doves... they've all flown away!
lines.dir: wailing, comic, flapping his arms like a bird

lines.zh: 耶稣爱上帝的家。后来病人来找他，他医好他们；小孩子们唱：和散那！
lines.en: Jesus loved God's house. Soon sick people came and He healed them, and children sang: 'Hosanna!'
lines.dir: warm, Jesus was not just angry: He loved God's house; lift into the children's 和散那 / 'Hosanna' at the end

lines.zh: 晚上，他们在楼上吃逾越节的晚餐。可是一路上，门徒们在争一件事……
lines.en: That evening they met upstairs for the Passover supper. But on the way, the disciples were arguing...
lines.dir: cosy evening voice, then a knowing little pause at the end

lines.zh: 等耶稣当了王，我要坐在他的右边！
lines.en: When Jesus is King, I'm going to sit on His right side!
lines.dir: puffed up, pleased with himself

lines.zh: 那我就坐左边！
lines.en: Then I'll sit on His left!
lines.dir: the youngest, quick and cheeky

lines.zh: 喂喂喂！我是第一个跟耶稣的，我才是最大的！
lines.en: Hey, hey, hey! I was the first one to follow Jesus. I'm the greatest!
lines.dir: big and loud, thumbs at his chest

lines.zh: 哥，其实……是我先带你去见耶稣的。
lines.en: Um, brother... actually, I'm the one who took you to meet Jesus.
lines.dir: mild, a little shy, deadpan; the joke is in how calm he is

lines.zh: 呃……那、那个不算！
lines.en: Er... that... that doesn't count!
lines.dir: caught out, flustered, comic

lines.zh: 平常会有仆人给客人洗脏脏的脚。可是今天晚上，谁也不愿意做仆人。
lines.en: Usually a servant washed the guests' dusty feet. But that night, nobody wanted to be the servant.
lines.dir: plain and gentle; a small sigh on 谁也不愿意 / 'nobody wanted'

lines.zh: 耶稣在腰上束了一条毛巾，把水倒进盆里……然后跪下来，给门徒洗脚。
lines.en: Jesus tied a towel round His waist, poured water into a bowl... then knelt down and began to wash their feet.
lines.dir: hushed, slow, with wonder; long pause at the dots

lines.zh: 老师……在给我们洗脚？
lines.en: The Teacher... is washing our feet?
lines.dir: a stunned whisper

lines.zh: 主啊，你要给我洗脚？不行！永远不行！
lines.en: Lord, You're going to wash MY feet? No! Never, ever!
lines.dir: shocked and embarrassed, hands up, pulling his feet back; loud

lines.zh: 彼得，我若不洗你，你就不能和我在一起了。
lines.en: Peter, if I don't wash you, you can't belong with Me.
lines.dir: very gentle, patient, looking up at him

lines.zh: 啊？那不光洗脚！手也洗，头也洗，全身都洗吧！
lines.en: What? Then not just my feet! My hands and my head too! Wash all of me!
lines.dir: all in at once, comic over-eagerness, voice rising

lines.zh: 哈哈，彼得，洗洗脚就够啦。
lines.en: Ha ha! Peter, your feet are enough.
lines.dir: a warm, real laugh; fond

lines.zh: 犹大也在这里；他已经决定背叛耶稣，耶稣知道，却还是给他洗了脚。
lines.en: Judas was there too; he had already turned against Jesus, yet Jesus washed his feet as well.
lines.dir: quiet and plain, no drama; a soft weight on 还是 / 'as well'

lines.zh: 你们叫我老师，叫我主。我给你们洗了脚，你们也要这样彼此服侍。
lines.en: You call Me Teacher and Lord. I washed your feet, so now you should serve each other too.
lines.dir: warm, clear, unhurried; to all four

lines.zh: 最大的人，要像仆人一样，帮助大家。
lines.en: The greatest one is the one who serves, like a helper to everyone.
lines.dir: simple and gentle, the heart of the story; slow

lines.zh: 吃晚饭的时候，耶稣拿起饼来，感谢上帝，把饼掰开，分给门徒。
lines.en: During supper, Jesus took the bread, thanked God for it, broke it, and gave it to His disciples.
lines.dir: reverent and simple; slow, each action its own beat

lines.zh: 这饼是我的身体，是为你们舍的。以后你们一起吃饼的时候，要记得我。
lines.en: This bread is My body, given for you. Whenever you eat it together, remember Me.
lines.dir: quiet, tender, deliberate; looking at each of them

lines.zh: 这杯是上帝新的约定。我要为你们舍命，让大家的罪得到赦免。
lines.en: This cup is God's new promise. I give My life for you, so that sins can be forgiven.
lines.dir: very gentle and calm; not sad, full of love

lines.zh: 王都给我洗脚了……安得烈，来，把脚伸出来——这回轮到我了！
lines.en: The King washed my feet... Andrew, come on, feet out! It's my turn now!
lines.dir: first slow and thoughtful, then a warm, cheerful decision

lines.zh: 哈哈，好痒！哥，你洗得比耶稣还慢！
lines.en: Ha ha, that tickles! Brother, you're even slower than Jesus!
lines.dir: giggling, teasing his big brother

lines.zh: 耶稣是最大的王，可他没有等别人来伺候他，他自己弯下腰，来服侍别人。
lines.en: Jesus is the greatest King of all. But He didn't wait for others to serve Him. He bent down and served them.
lines.dir: warm moral, straight to the child; slow and clear

lines.zh: 你也可以像耶稣一样：帮忙摆碗筷，让朋友先玩。爱帮助别人的，才是真正的大人物！
lines.en: You can serve like Jesus too: help set the table, let a friend go first. Helpers are the truly great ones!
lines.dir: encouraging, a smile; lift on 真正的大人物 / 'truly great'
